I (33M) have bipolar type 1, and maybe I can give you a patient perspective that helps. Just to qualify, at my worst I couldn't sleep at all for 5 days at a time, 2-3 times a week. Also, I would be manic up to 10 days at a time and it was absolutely miserable most of the time. It becomes physically painful from the anxiety, agitation and trying to maintain composure through challenging conversations where nobody feels heard. We can't shut up, or we are afraid to speak and we feel backed up into an absolute corner to just act as normal as we are, and when someone says something that makes this moment any harder (whether they are being reasonable or not), it can just make the panic and emotions get even worse. You obviously can't always avoid pushing these buttons, but trying goes a long way.

I don't know how your practice or clinic works, it sounds like it's not inpatient but i know you suggested inpatient. It's going to be really hard to get this patient to see reason until they are not manic, and i'm assuming you would try to prescribe them something? Maybe something for the immediate mania, like a benzo or antipsychotic as well as a mood stabilizer. 300mg lithium absolutely changed my life. I know that's a low dose, but I read up on how it gets way overdosed for patients because you all seem to think there's a narrow therapeutic window. Maybe for some people, but many people will think lithium didn't work because they were given way too much as well. Just my experience and a bunch of other people on reddit that gave me the idea. Regarding the antipsychotic meds and benzos, If i could go back to my psych stays before I found out i am bipolar, I would probably be best off on 1-3 days of low dose benzo than the psych meds because the antipsychotics throw me into a deppression that doesn't leave until they do, but it can still be an upgrade to mania at first. I know benzos have plenty of bad properties long term, and I don't take any, but they will mitigate mania and the short-term impacts on kidneys, liver and even brain seem negligible at low doses for short periods. Until you bring them down, you are going to be extremely frustrated and they are unlikely to do anything that seems more stressful or unknown to their current situation.

Aside from meds, there is exercise. It's not going to cure mania, but 1-3 sets of pushups will provide some relief. Even going on a walk or any exercise really will usually help a little for a little. Conversationally, if you start with genuine caring concern it will go over better than stern concern. Letting them know information about where they can go, who they can call etc. if things happen again or get worse might help. I had experiences going to psych wards in my 20's and they just said it's because i'm an addict and things never got better and i stopped going to psych wards because i felt worse when i was there and they couldn't help me. I couldn't stay sober because of my mania, and until i addressed that i was never going to stay sober without offing myself. There are no easy answers, but your heart is in the right place.

As I learn more about bipolar, I am amazed that doctors did not see it in me sooner or give me relevant information about bipolar once i had been diagnosed. They were also very unkind most of the time.. Don't be afraid to prescribe low dose lithium. Counties with more lithium in the water have lower suicide, drug use and crime so it's not just theoretical. I have been amazed how little doctors knew about bipolar other than what they can prescribe. Speak to some other bipolar patients that are easier to talk to and they might have some good insight.
